title: a re-export is a module edge: re-exporting from an untrusted foreign module needs the same initialization trust claim an import does
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Runtime TypeScript Dependency' (Locked). A re-export executes the target module's initializer in exactly the way an import does — that is what the initialization trust claim guards against — so the rule cannot be attached to the `import` keyword. This is the smallest possible statement of that, and it is here because before this revision ZERO of the corpus's `.sm` files contained a re-export in any area: `export … from` and `export *` appeared nowhere, so the entire re-export surface of the language was uncontracted. Nothing in the file reads the binding, so the single declared diagnostic is the module-edge rule with no call or property cascade on top of it. Its companion is 21-native-pin/a-pin-reaching-a-host-module-through-a-re-export-is-rejected, which pins what the same edge does to a native pin one module further away. RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to compile this program clean and run it — zero diagnostics and `done` on stdout — where the reference reports SMITHERS1510@5:30 at the re-export. The cause recorded on the marker was that no export declaration was ever examined for a module edge (`grep -n IsExportDeclaration compiler/forkbridge/*.go.txt` returned nothing), so the trust rule was one keyword away from being unenforced. The fork's `staticRuntimeModuleEdge` now owns runtime export declarations as well as imports (compiler/forkbridge/nativepin.go.txt); measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`.
